To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the presence of a predator can alter prey behavior and (2) the presence of predators can select for behavioral differences between populations of the same species

(1) facultative behavioral responses by prey can evolve rapidly in response to consistent presence or absence in predation, (2) facultative behavioral changes by prey can evolve in response to consistent absence in predation but not to inconsistent presence or absence of a predator, (3) facultative behavioral shifts can persist in prey in the absence of a predator but may disappear in prey that have been consistently preyed upon by a predator.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary consequences of interactions between predators and prey.
the effects of predation on the evolution of prey behavioral responses.
understanding the ecological processes that maintain genetic variation in natural populations and the genetic processes that generate and maintain that variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
predation can select for rapid evolution of prey behaviour, and that this evolution can be in the form of both facultative and obligate changes in behaviour.
The presence of predation can cause prey to change its behaviour.
the presence of predators can select rapidly for divergent behavior in prey, including the facultative behavioral response of prey to predators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence or absence of a predator can select for divergence in prey behavioral responses to predators.
predation can select quickly for behavioral change and that behavioral change can be selected quickly by predation.

predation can cause rapid evolution in prey behavior and that the evolution of prey responses to predators can be predicted from the relative costs of the different prey behaviors and their relative benefits in the presence and absence of predators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prey can evolve behavioral defenses against predation.
prey can evolve to be more or less responsive to predators in different environments.
the presence of a predator can select for rapid divergence in prey behavior.
